chunks: And God knows your enemies well, and sufficient is God as a protector, and sufficient is God as a helper.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that God is sufficient as a Wali and Nasir?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of divine sufficiency (Kifayah), reassuring believers that God’s knowledge of their adversaries surpasses their own, thereby validating reliance on Him alone. It underscores the dual role of Allah as both the ultimate protector (Wali) and the source of victory (Nasir), a theme frequently cited in supplications for spiritual and political resilience.
